newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress confirms support for govt withdrawn.
newsitem.headline: India Congress confirms support for govt withdrawn.

text.p: The leader of India's Congress party on Sunday confirmed he had withdrawn support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition government.

Asked to confirm a news agency report that the Congress had decided to withdraw support to Deve Gowda's nine-month-old government, Sitaram Kesri told Reuters: "Yes. It has been done." He refused to elaborate.
Kamaluddin Ahmed, a Congress leader, when asked if the party's withdrawal of support meant a snap mid-term national election, said: "Don't be silly. We will form our own government."
Government officials were not immediately available for comment.

Deve Gowda's minority United Front alliance controls some 178 deputies in the 545-member Lok Sabha or lower house. The Congress, which supported the government but was not part of the ruling alliance and holds no cabinet posts, has 142 deputies.
A Congress spokesman said the party had called a news conference at 4:00 p.m. (1030 GMT).
